# R8 — Suffering and Death (22:1–23:56) + Exaltation (24:1–53)

**Range read in full:** raw 9913–10757 (slice complete, 845 lines)  
**Source:** Green, *The Gospel of Luke* (NICNT, 1997)  
**Section:** §7 The Suffering and Death of Jesus (22:1–23:56); §8 The Exaltation of Jesus (24:1–53)  
**Target slugs (for integration):** [[luke]], [[joel-green]], [[jesus]], [[peter-apostle]], [[acts]], [[luke-acts-unity]], [[new-covenant]]

## Claims

### C1 — Passion plot driven by conflict; people as buffer that must be breached
**Locus:** 9913–9921 (slice ll. 1–9)  
**Quote:** "the most pervasive and important of which is the motif of conflict… Luke’s narration has repeatedly established the important place of “the people” as a buffer between Jesus and his opposition… a barrier that must now be breached if the Jerusalem leadership is to have its way with him."  
**Claim (Green):** Passion is continuous with earlier conflict (Simeon 2:34; John; Jesus). Jerusalem setting + Passover festival charge the drama; “the people” have buffered Jesus from leaders—breach of that barrier is structural to the passion plot.

### C2 — Unholy alliances made and unmade; Satan–leadership–Judas; disciples falter then separate
**Locus:** 9923–9925 (slice ll. 11–13)  
**Quote:** "the Lukan account of Jesus’ passion and death is in part the story of unholy alliances made and unmade… Satan and the Jerusalem leadership are allied… through diabolic influence… Judas… Peter… denying his Lord three times… eventual separation from those who oppose Jesus—first… Peter… then… the others (23:49). The only exception is Judas, whose place among the twelve must be filled by another (Acts 1:15–26)."  
**Claim (Green):** Alliances breach the buffer (Satan+leaders; Judas; crowds/people join leaders 23:4, 13–14) then fray (Peter’s remorse; daughters of Jerusalem; people watching not scoffing; crowds beating breasts). Judas alone is not restored—[[acts]] replacement. Links [[peter-apostle]], [[luke-acts-unity]].

### C3 — Tragic irony: opponents think they serve God, serve diabolic aim; war of interpretation
**Locus:** 9927–9931 (slice ll. 15–19)  
**Quote:** "Those who oppose Jesus believe themselves to be serving God, yet unwittingly serve a diabolic aim… war of interpretation: Who understands and serves the divine aim, really?… Because both Jerusalem authorities and Jesus see themselves as acting on behalf of the divine will, the actions that unfold in chs. 22–23 are indeed tragic."  
**Claim (Green):** Passion is fullest manifestation of competing aims (cf. wilderness temptation 4:1–13). Jesus is exemplar in trial, not merely prototypical martyr—death of the Righteous/Servant/prophet, Son of Man, Royal Messiah, servant-benefactor, all “grounded in divine necessity, foreordained by God and foretold in the Scriptures.”

### C4 — Unlikely recognizers of Jesus’ identity at the cross
**Locus:** 9933–9935 (slice ll. 21–23)  
**Quote:** "Simon… surrogate disciple… women from the city mourn… A condemned-and-crucified criminal comprehends Jesus’ righteousness and status as heir to the kingdom… a Gentile centurion recognizes Jesus as the Righteous One… Joseph of Arimathea… exemplary piety."  
**Claim (Green):** Christology grasped by outsiders; passion is theologically grounded—God faithful to prayer, angelic fortitude, trust for vindication (22:16, 18; 23:43).

### C5 — Last Supper unit: form (farewell discourse) + Passover–kingdom correlation
**Locus:** 9937–9951 (slice ll. 25–39)  
**Quote:** "crucial for understanding both the form and content of vv 1–38 is its orientation around a meal… literary form, the “farewell discourse”… Luke accents the identification of this meal as a Passover… Passover places its stamp on the meaning of the kingdom, while the Passover finds itself fulfilled in the kingdom."  
**Claim (Green):** §7.1 is meal-centered farewell (gathering, prediction of death, exhortation, review of life, prophecies, warnings)—not mere symposium. Exodus motifs: liberation of oppressed; sacrifice/covenant; Yahweh’s kingship → “kingdom of God”; Passover ritual anticipating new exodus. All “brought to completion through the death of Jesus… eschatological banquet.”

### C6 — Conspiracy: human stratagem + Satan’s entry into Judas
**Locus:** 9953–9971 (slice ll. 41–59)  
**Quote:** "More is at work than human schemes… Luke credits Satan with providing necessary intervention… linguistic connection between 4:13 and 22:6… the “opportune time” for which Satan was waiting… Judas… room for human volition… “rule of mammon”… temple… interests… in conflict with Jesus."  
**Claim (Green):** Parallel “how kill / how betray” + fear of people / no crowd. Cosmic dimension (cf. Qumran Angel of Darkness quoted as worldview parallel—Green secondary illustration). Leaders’ “greatly pleased” perverts normal Lukan “rejoice” at salvation. Echoes Suffering Righteous constellation.

### C7 — Passover preparation: δεῖ of lamb sacrifice parallels necessity of Jesus’ suffering; Jesus active agent
**Locus:** 9973–9985 (slice ll. 61–73)  
**Quote:** "Luke’s attribution of the timing of sacrifice to divine necessity… the necessity of the Passover sacrifice parallels and anticipates the necessity of Jesus’ suffering… Jesus is himself an active agent… no helpless victim… Peter and John… exemplary disciples… table servants… anticipate their roles as leaders in… Acts… fictive kin group… head of a “household.”"  
**Claim (Green):** Dual compulsion—Torah/divine timetable + Jesus’ prophetic foresight (cf. entry 19:28–34). Contrast Judas vs Peter/John. Links [[peter-apostle]], [[acts]].

### C8 — Table teaching: death interpreted by divine purpose and Scripture; dual identity of Jesus and disciples
**Locus:** 9987–9991 (slice ll. 75–79)  
**Quote:** "Jesus holds together his own identity and fate with that of his disciples… Behind them stands the purpose of God, predetermined and evident in the Scriptures of Israel (vv 21, 37)."  
**Claim (Green):** Farewell + Passover + covenant-making escalate boundary-making; servant authority and trials for both Jesus and disciples.

### C9 — Passover cup/bread: kingdom future fulfillment; body given / new covenant in blood
**Locus:** 9993–10033 (slice ll. 81–121)  
**Quote:** "I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God… This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood… “new covenant” is drawn from Jer 31:31–34… “covenant in my blood,” one may hear an allusion to Exod 24:8… Jesus’ death is said to atone for the sins of the people… extended… to all who embrace “good news to the poor.”"  
**Claim (Green):** Passover not self-interpreting—every detail explained (kingdom or death). “Apostles” as representatives of God’s people. Remembrance = efficacious re-appropriation of Jesus’ table lifestyle (justice, service), not mere cognitive recall. Breaking bread not itself symbolic of manner of death; distribution = giving life. Continuity of new with old covenant in Luke’s frame. **Note (Green):** substitutionary cross rare in Acts mission sermons (only Acts 20:28); exaltation more pervasive for salvation. Target: [[new-covenant]], [[jesus]], [[luke]].

### C10 — Post-resurrection meals do not “fulfill” Passover; kingdom consummation still future
**Locus:** 10019–10021 (slice ll. 107–109)  
**Quote:** "Acts does not record the consummation of the kingdom of God—which, then, remains a future reality… They do not constitute the “fulfillment of Passover,” but should nevertheless draw into the present… meal sharing as… celebration and eschatological anticipation."  
**Claim (Green):** Meals in Acts retain eschatological anticipation; exaltation as enthronement (Acts 2) does not collapse future kingdom.

### C11 — Betrayer at table: dual causation (δεῖ / determined) + human woe
**Locus:** 10035–10045 (slice ll. 123–133)  
**Quote:** "the Son of Man is going as it has been determined, but woe to that one by whom he is betrayed… transparent affirmation of the larger biblical notion of dual causation… death is not the full realization of the divine plan, only a necessary component… followed by vindication and royal dominion."  
**Claim (Green):** Any apostle could be the betrayer from table perspective; Ps 41:9 reverberation; hand/power of opponents even at Passover. Divine sovereignty and responsibility held together.

### C12 — Status dispute as collective betrayal of kingdom values; servant leadership vs Gentile benefaction system
**Locus:** 10047–10071 (slice ll. 135–159)  
**Quote:** "all twelve of them “betray” his basic kingdom message… “But not so with you”… manner of ruling and benefaction must be utterly transformed… I am among you as one who serves… You are those who have stood by me in my trials; and I confer on you… a kingdom… sit on thrones ruling the twelve tribes of Israel."  
**Claim (Green):** Reversal: greatest = youngest/server; critique of Greco-Roman benefaction as system of status legitimation, not only its abuses. Apostles share Jesus’ kingdom (still his table/kingship); leadership transfer typical of farewell; Judas’s inclusion left open until Acts 1. Restoration of Israel governance via “apostles.”

### C13 — Satan sifts all; Jesus prays for Peter; turn back and strengthen brothers
**Locus:** 10073–10095 (slice ll. 161–183)  
**Quote:** "Satan has demanded to sift all of you like wheat, but I have prayed for you that your own faith may not fail; and you, when once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers and sisters… Reversion to… “Simon”… identity and vocation as an apostle are at stake… Peter is later portrayed as the emerging leader… Acts 1:15–26."  
**Claim (Green):** Job-like sifting; Satan inspires faithlessness. Prayer for Peter benefits the group; “turn” ≈ repentance (cf. Acts 26:18). Peter’s bravado first grasps Jesus is about to die. Links [[peter-apostle]], [[acts]].

### C14 — “But now”: hospitality → hostility; sword metaphorical; Isa 53:12 “lawless”
**Locus:** 10097–10109 (slice ll. 185–197)  
**Quote:** "But now, the one who has a purse must take it… sword… metaphorical reference to the coming reality… “It is enough!”… exasperation… this scripture must be fulfilled in me, ‘And he was counted among the lawless’… more probably… friendship with sinners… adversaries who do the reckoning… continuous present (“is being fulfilled”)."  
**Claim (Green):** Mission conditions change radically; violent sword-reading negated by 22:49–51. Form of Jesus’ life inseparable from death; disciples face same pattern. Fulfillment language: scripture + δεῖ + fulfilled (2x).

### C15 — Mount of Olives: watershed of passion; prayer vs trial; not martyr bravado
**Locus:** 10111–10125 (slice ll. 199–213)  
**Quote:** "Jesus’ struggle on the Mount of Olives is presented by Luke as the watershed in the passion narrative… unreserved allegiance to God… not… prototypical martyr… More suggestive… Isaianic Servant… suffering as… divine will, submissive obedience… angelic… aid… inclusio of vv 40 and 46."  
**Claim (Green):** Parenetic: pray lest enter trial (diabolic). Structure A–B–A′ prayer (Father’s will / remove cup / your will). Cup = calamity/death. Angel strengthens for more earnest prayer, does not remove cup. Irony: obedience to God also accepts fate Satan wills—unfolding shows death is devil’s demise. Disciples sleep from grief—failure not final/fatal.

### C16 — Arrest: Jesus masters the scene; healing enemy’s ear; “your hour… power of darkness”
**Locus:** 10127–10175 (slice ll. 215–263)  
**Quote:** "in spite of appearances, he is the true master… No more of this!… touched his ear and healed him… this is your hour, and the power of darkness… temple authorities as instruments of Satan… collusion between Judas and the temple leadership."  
**Claim (Green):** Crowd identity delayed for rhetoric (positive “crowd” → hostile leaders). Disciples’ sword attempt = dullness after no prayer. Healing enacts love of enemies, anticipates 23:34, proves Jesus no “bandit.” Diabolic hour coincides with leaders’ hour.

### C17 — Peter’s denial fulfills prophecy; “word of the Lord”; weeping as turning
**Locus:** 10177–10201 (slice ll. 265–289)  
**Quote:** "his role… primarily related to demonstrating that Jesus is truly a prophet… The Lord turned and looked at Peter… “the word of the Lord”… weeping marks the beginning of Peter’s “turning”… failure… not absolute… recovery… Acts 4–5… boldness."  
**Claim (Green):** Escalating denials dismantle Petrine identity (know Jesus → association → Galilean beginning). Juxtaposition “Lord” + “word of the Lord” = Jesus more than prophet—divine agency. Mockery “Prophesy!” ironic. Abuse by arresting leaders; possible blasphemy sense. Links [[peter-apostle]], [[jesus]].

### C18 — Trial unit: double irony of Jewish leaders; four scenes; “their voices prevailed”
**Locus:** 10203–10221 (slice ll. 291–309)  
**Quote:** "even these decisions… outworking of the ancient divine purpose… double irony… opposing Jesus they are actually opposing… divine purpose… yet… instrumentality in Jesus’ crucifixion… serves that plan… “their voices prevailed” (23:23)… not… exonerate the Romans."  
**Claim (Green):** Sanhedrin → Pilate → Herod → sentencing. Leaders constant catalyst. People temporarily complicit. Rome declares innocence but refuses true identity of Jesus as ruler; Pilate’s flog-and-release = political expediency. False-prophet charge (Deut 13) translated into royal/sedition terms for Rome. Jesus = regal prophet, Messiah, Son of God.

### C19 — Sanhedrin: Messiah/Son of God questions; “from now on” Son of Man at God’s right hand
**Locus:** 10223–10243 (slice ll. 311–331)  
**Quote:** "If you are the Messiah, tell us… from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God… Are you, then, the Son of God?… You say that I am… Jesus turns their accusation… into an unwitting confession!"  
**Claim (Green):** Questions echo devil’s “If you are Son of God” (4:3, 9); diabolic collocation. Unbelief predicted. Ps 110:1 enthronement prolepsis; “power of God” vs “power of darkness.” Messiah and Son of God virtually same for Luke. Fulfills 9:22 necessity of rejection by these groups.

### C20 — Pilate: one charge “perverting the nation”; innocence declared; religio-political, not pro-Roman whitewash
**Locus:** 10245–10285 (slice ll. 333–373)  
**Quote:** "only one charge… “We found this man perverting our nation”… elaborations… taxes… Messiah, a king… I find no basis for an accusation… purpose… not primarily to have Rome establish Jesus’ innocence… Jewish leadership presses its case… leading eventually to Jesus’ execution."  
**Claim (Green):** Distinctions “religious vs political” anachronistic. Charges intelligible; partly true (Messiah; relativized tribute; leading Israel) but twisted. Jesus turns Pilate’s king question into ironic affirmation as at 22:70. “Crowds” with Pilate = sanhedrin members here. Leaders, not Jesus, stir up the people.

### C21 — Herod: silence (Servant); mock royal robe; friendship with Pilate against Jesus (Acts 4)
**Locus:** 10287–10307 (slice ll. 375–395)  
**Quote:** "Rome’s aversion to acting with justice… Jesus gave him no answer… Servant of Yahweh… (Isa 53:7)… elegant robe… ironic mockery… Herod and Pilate became friends… Acts 4:26–27… gathered together in opposition against “your holy servant Jesus.”"  
**Claim (Green):** Herod fails to see/hear (sign-seeking 11:16, 29–30). Contempt accumulation, not honor. Roman rulers join hostility. Links [[acts]], [[luke-acts-unity]].

### C22 — Sentencing: triple Pilate release attempt; Jesus vs Barabbas; voices prevail
**Locus:** 10309–10343 (slice ll. 397–431)  
**Quote:** "threefold attempt of Pilate to effect Jesus’ release… “their voices prevailed”… handed Jesus over as they wished… You rejected the Holy and Righteous One and asked to have a murderer given to you … (Acts 3:13–14)."  
**Claim (Green):** Innocence motif intensified (find nothing / no evil). People first join leaders explicitly. Barabbas foil—insurrectionist rightly for cross. Pilate assuages mob, not justice. Flogging of innocent = favor-seeking. Links [[jesus]] righteousness theme for Acts speeches.

### C23 — Way of the cross: Simon as cross-bearing discipleship; daughters of Jerusalem oracle
**Locus:** 10345–10395 (slice ll. 433–483)  
**Quote:** "Simon of Cyrene… carry it behind Jesus… reminder of the nature of discipleship… Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves… if they do this when the wood is green, what will happen when it is dry?"  
**Claim (Green):** Ambiguous “they” = Rome+leaders+people solidarity, then segregation begins. Judgment on Jerusalem for rejecting visitation (19:41–44; Hos 10:8); mourning can open to repentance—not inevitable destruction for all inhabitants. Cross-bearing echoes 9:23; 14:27.

### C24 — Crucifixion mockery phases; Savior ironically from the cross; Ps 22/69 Scripture frame
**Locus:** 10397–10431 (slice ll. 485–519)  
**Quote:** "three phases of mockery… leaders… soldiers… criminal… From the cross, he asks God to extend forgiveness… promises salvation… royal status and his role as Savior are interconnected… with the necessity of Jesus’ suffering… crucifixion seals the identity of Jesus as the Messiah and king who accomplishes the divine purpose precisely as the suffering one."  
**Claim (Green):** Father, forgive them—Jews and Romans; ignorance motif for Acts; love of enemies (6:27–28). Lots for clothing = Ps 22:18 humiliation + divine foresight. Leaders’ titles (Messiah, Chosen One Isa 42:1) correct but wrongly collated with self-deliverance criterion. Inscription ironic truth of kingship. Sour wine ~ Ps 69:21.

### C25 — Penitent criminal: innocence recognized; “today… Paradise”; death not contradiction of messiahship
**Locus:** 10433–10439 (slice ll. 521–527)  
**Quote:** "this man has done nothing wrong… remember me when you come into your kingdom… today you will be with me in Paradise… first to recognize that Jesus’ crucifixion is a precursor to his enthronement… God’s plan comes to fruition through, not in spite of, the crucifixion."  
**Claim (Green):** Paradise = God’s garden/new creation; “today” = Lukan immediacy of salvation (4:21; 19:9). Criminal is reliable hermeneut ratified by Jesus. Not Green’s preferred reading of Isa 53:12 as criminals beside him (cf. C14).

### C26 — Death portents: darkness (last days / diabolic) and temple veil (divine passive)
**Locus:** 10441–10453 (slice ll. 529–541)  
**Quote:** "darkness came over the whole land… the curtain of the temple was torn in two… divine passive… God’s turning away from the temple… neutralizing the centrality of the temple in preparation for the centrifugal mission… “end of the earth” (Acts 1:8)."  
**Claim (Green):** Veil ≠ temple destruction (temple still used in early Acts); symbolizes dismantling of temple’s socio-religious segregation world. Darkness: diabolic + Joel/Amos Day of the Lord + Acts 2 universal mission. Causation chain: portents → death → responses.

### C27 — Jesus dies entrusting spirit (Ps 31:5); faith in God who raises
**Locus:** 10453–10455 (slice ll. 541–543)  
**Quote:** "Father, into your hands I commend my spirit… Ps 31:5… Suffering Righteous One… faith in the God who raises from the dead."  
**Claim (Green):** Dual Father address from cross; death congruent with Sonship; presence of God in darkness.

### C28 — Centurion: “righteous” = innocence + Suffering Righteous + Isaianic Servant; crowds mourn
**Locus:** 10457–10481 (slice ll. 545–569)  
**Quote:** "Certainly this man was righteous… Suffering Righteous One… Isaianic Servant… Acts 3:13–14… dual identification of Jesus as Messiah and Servant… crowds… beating their breasts… prepares for their repentance and faith in the early chapters of Acts."  
**Claim (Green):** Witness motif (saw/spectacle/watching). Gentile + Jewish responses proleptic of Simeon 2:30–32. Acquaintances/women stand at distance—weakened discipleship tension (Ps 38:11); women continuity for resurrection memory. Links [[acts]], [[jesus]].

### C29 — Burial: Joseph righteous council member against council’s “plan”; honorable burial; women keep law
**Locus:** 10483–10503 (slice ll. 571–591)  
**Quote:** "good and righteous man… not agreed to their plan and action… waiting expectantly for the kingdom of God… tale of two competing purposes… women… rested according to the commandment… Israel expresses its faithfulness most fully when it is oriented toward Jesus."  
**Claim (Green):** No blanket condemnation of Judaism; division within Israel (2:34–35). Joseph like birth-narrative pious figures. Burial honors surpass criminal norm; Sabbath inclusio bridges to resurrection.

---

### C30 — Luke 24 as climax and bridge: exaltation focus; Luke 24 // Acts 1 internal repetition
**Locus:** 10505–10537 (slice ll. 593–625)  
**Quote:** "Luke 24 and Acts 1 provide the transition… from the story of Jesus to the story of his witnesses… internal repetition… appearance… eating… remain in Jerusalem… Father’s promise… “witnesses”… universal… ascension… Gospel is incomplete in itself… requires… Acts."  
**Claim (Green):** Three anticipated moments: ascension (here), Spirit baptism (Acts 2), parousia (not narrated). Open threads: full salvation to all, Israel’s response, Spirit gift, parousia—retaken in Acts 1:1–11. Cross/empty tomb not self-interpreting. Links [[luke-acts-unity]], [[acts]].

### C31 — Hermeneutical rules of ch. 24: Jesus’ words + Israel’s Scriptures; mutual interpretation
**Locus:** 10537–10541 (slice ll. 625–629)  
**Quote:** "Jesus’ own words as God’s regal prophet are thus key… continuous with the Scriptures of Israel… Jesus as the one who both interprets and actualizes… Scriptures… not self-interpreting… By means of the resurrection, Jesus’ perspective… authorized by God… He must also enable them properly to read the Scriptures."  
**Claim (Green):** Passion fulfills status/mission; resurrection/ascension = vindication; “everything written” fruition. Setting: Jerusalem bookends Gospel.

### C32 — Empty tomb: angels recall δεῖ of Son of Man; women remember; men dismiss as idle tale
**Locus:** 10543–10597 (slice ll. 631–685)  
**Quote:** "Why do you look for the living among the dead?… Son of Man must be handed over to sinners, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again… Then they remembered his words… idle tale, and they did not believe them… Peter… amazed… not yet faith."  
**Claim (Green):** Empty tomb irrelevant once “He is not here”; interpretation key = Jesus’ prior teaching. Women spontaneous witnesses (no commission); male bias against women witnesses. “Lord Jesus” prolepsis of Acts exaltation confession. Peter advances but falls short of women. Links [[peter-apostle]].

### C33 — Emmaus: eyes kept from recognizing; dashed hopes of redeeming Israel; prophet-like-Moses incomplete
**Locus:** 10599–10663 (slice ll. 687–751)  
**Quote:** "their eyes were kept from recognizing him… we had hoped that he was the one to redeem Israel… prophet mighty in deed and word… prophet-like-Moses… What is lacking… destiny of the prophets: rejection, suffering, and death… more… regal prophet… correlation of suffering and messiahship."  
**Claim (Green):** Journey motif reopens 9:45/18:34 obtuseness. Cleopas irony: only Jesus “knows.” Summary affirms Lukan portrait yet misses suffering pattern and messianic surplus over prophet. “Third day” raw material unused.

### C34 — Emmaus key: δεῖ that Messiah suffer then enter glory; Moses and all prophets interpret “the things”
**Locus:** 10663–10669 (slice ll. 751–757)  
**Quote:** "Was it not necessary that the Messiah should suffer these things and then enter into his glory?… beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he interpreted… all the scriptures… shift… Son of Man or the prophets who “must suffer”… to… the Messiah who “must suffer”… hermeneutical innovation… eschatological king who would suffer before entering his glory."  
**Claim (Green):** “Foolish/slow of heart” = dispositional failure, not mere info gap. Suffering messiahship = status-reversal soteriology; death = center of divine-human struggle over humility vs self-glorification. Scripture and Jesus’ career mutually informing.

### C35 — Recognition at bread-breaking; not primarily eucharistic; return to Jerusalem; Simon appearance
**Locus:** 10671–10681 (slice ll. 759–769)  
**Quote:** "took bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it… eyes were opened… closest parallels… 9:12–17… not… Last Supper… The Lord has risen indeed, and he has appeared to Simon!… full rehabilitation… leader of the community of witnesses… bridge from table fellowship… to… Acts (e.g., Acts 2:46)."  
**Claim (Green):** Hospitality + meal as revelation site; host role shifts. Scriptural opening and bread-breaking dual moments (v 35). Unnarrated appearance to Simon legitimates [[peter-apostle]] post-denial. Breaking of bread = meal itself, salvation nearness in Acts. Spontaneous witness without commission. Links [[acts]], [[luke-acts-unity]].

### C36 — Appearance: embodied resurrection—flesh, bones, fish; not ghost or mere immortal soul
**Locus:** 10683–10709 (slice ll. 771–797)  
**Quote:** "a ghost does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have… ate in their presence… rules out any notion of the resuscitation of a corpse… excludes… merely an ethereal event… material data… insufficient… scriptural illumination is added."  
**Claim (Green):** Angelophany shape with contrasts. “Peace” metonymic for salvation after cross. Joy-caused disbelief (“too good to be true”). Seeing for authentic future witness (v 48). Continuity of pre- and post-resurrection identity: “It is I myself!”

### C37 — Scripture opened: Messiah suffer + rise + repentance for forgiveness to all nations from Jerusalem
**Locus:** 10711–10733 (slice ll. 799–821)  
**Quote:** "everything written about me in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms must be fulfilled… Messiah is to suffer and to rise… repentance for forgiveness of sins is to be proclaimed in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem. You are witnesses… what my Father promised… clothed with power from on high."  
**Claim (Green):** Three infinitives sew Israel–Jesus–church stories. Psalms added for passion interpretation. Not verse-hunting but whole-Scripture truth; Isa 49:6 under mission (Luke 2:32; Acts 13:47; 1:8). Centripetal Zion expectation reversed → centrifugal mission (veil effects). Witnesses empowered by Spirit; Jesus (not only Father) sends Spirit (cf. 3:16; Acts 1–2). Jerusalem stay tests obedience. Bridge to [[acts]]; [[luke-acts-unity]]; [[new-covenant]] forgiveness theme continued.

### C38 — Ascension: blessing (testamentary leave-taking); carried up; worship of Jesus; temple joy and obedience
**Locus:** 10735–10757 (slice ll. 823–845)  
**Quote:** "lifting up his hands, he blessed them… carried up into heaven… they worshiped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy… continually in the temple blessing God… ascent… prelude to the outpouring of the Spirit… continuity… Jesus who suffered… same who is carried up… to exercise royal power… between the ministry of Jesus and the mission of the early church."  
**Claim (Green):** Temporal link to “third day” left open (exploited in Acts 1). Bethany/Mount of Olives bookends entry. Priestly parallels (Lev 9; Sir 50) secondary—Luke not otherwise priestly Jesus; model = Moses/Abraham farewell blessing. Heavenward = glorified status; God’s verdict reverses executioners’. Worship of Jesus unique/climactic (only God may be worshiped in Luke-Acts). Joy/praise/obedience inclusio with birth narrative; wait for Spirit. Links [[jesus]], [[acts]], [[luke-acts-unity]].

### C39 — Nature of messianic suffering: through suffering purpose fulfilled; not denial of Sonship/kingship
**Locus:** 10351–10353, 10411–10413, 10667–10669 (slice ll. 439–441, 511–513, 755–757)  
**Quote:** "It is through suffering that Jesus fulfills the divine purpose… From the cross Jesus twice addresses God… as Father, confirming that he regards his passion as fully congruent with his status as God’s Son… in his suffering and resurrection, Jesus embodied the fullness of salvation interpreted as status reversal."  
**Claim (Green synthesis in-range):** Mockers make self-rescue criterion of messiahship; Lukan counter: salvation for others, forgiveness, Paradise “today,” Servant/righteous path, then glory. Suffering is constitutive of messianic vocation, not its negation.

### C40 — Innocence motif as through-line of trials and cross
**Locus:** 10317–10341, 10433–10439, 10457–10469 (slice ll. 405–429, 521–527, 545–557)  
**Quote:** "focus attention on the innocence of Jesus… he has done nothing wrong… Certainly this man was righteous… intensity of this emphasis on Jesus’ innocence is important for Luke’s overall portrayal of Jesus as the righteous one who suffers and will be vindicated."  
**Claim (Green):** Pilate (3x), Herod’s return, second criminal, centurion, and Acts 3:13–14 chain the innocence/righteousness theme from trial through death into apostolic preaching.

### C41 — Divine necessity (δεῖ) and Scripture fulfillment concentrated in passion–exaltation
**Locus:** 9931, 9981–9983, 10043–10045, 10105–10107, 10663–10667, 10711–10715 (slice ll. 19, 69–71, 131–133, 193–195, 751–755, 799–803)  
**Quote:** "grounded in divine necessity, foreordained by God and foretold in the Scriptures… Son of Man is going as it has been determined… this scripture must be fulfilled in me… Was it not necessary that the Messiah should suffer… everything written about me… must be fulfilled."  
**Claim (Green): δεῖ / determined / fulfilled language saturates supper (betrayal; Isa 53:12), empty tomb (must be handed over), Emmaus (Messiah must suffer), and final teaching (Moses–prophets–psalms). Human schemes and satanic hour are nested inside, not outside, divine purpose—without canceling culpability (dual causation; Acts speeches).

### C42 — Spirit promise and Jerusalem base as narrative hinge to Acts
**Locus:** 10519–10535, 10725–10733, 10745–10753 (slice ll. 607–623, 813–821, 833–841)  
**Quote:** "directive to remain in Jerusalem… prospective fulfillment of the Father’s promise… description of disciples as “witnesses”… stay here in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high… They… returned to Jerusalem… continually in the temple."  
**Claim (Green):** Gospel ends with obedient Jerusalem base and open Spirit promise; empowerment for witness is the missing resolution only Acts supplies. Ascension enables Jesus’ dispensing of the Spirit (Acts 2:32–33). Core [[luke-acts-unity]] claim.

### C43 — Farewell table as new-covenant actualization and servant paradigm for leadership
**Locus:** 9947–9951, 10029–10033, 10055–10067 (slice ll. 35–39, 117–121, 143–155)  
**Quote:** "actualizes a new covenant and exemplifies his servant role among them in his death… This cup… is the new covenant in my blood… the leader like one who serves… I am among you as one who serves."  
**Claim (Green):** Covenant sacrifice (Jer 31 + Exod 24 typology) and servant leadership co-define the farewell meal; table practice becomes ethical memory and leadership template for the post-Easter community (and Acts benefaction/healing). Targets: [[new-covenant]], [[jesus]], [[luke]].
